title: [CRY-4] KeyPackage init keys are described as coming from the long-term DID `keyAgreement` key
description: Review finding CRY-4: KeyPackage init keys are described as coming from the long-term DID `keyAgreement` key (lens CRY). Location: spec/02-identity.md:44, spec/02-identity.md:74, spec/02-identity.md:314. Fix: RFC 9420 §10 (rfc9420.txt, Key Packages) requires that init_key "MUST be unique among the set of KeyPackages created by this client". 02:44, 02:74 and 02:314 describe the DID `keyAgreement` key as the "source" of init keys. This is downgraded from P1 because the spec elsewhere contradicts a reuse reading. 05:67 says "reuse lets two groups share HPKE init secrets", and 05:117 forbids giving groups "the same HPKE init key". So the defect is contradictory text, not mandated reuse. Fix as proposed: init_key and leaf encryption_key are fresh per KeyPackage and unrelated to the DID document; `keyAgreement` serves only out-of-group HPKE. 06:345 (recorder archive sealing to the recorder's `keyAgreement` key) is a legitimate out-of-group use and needs no change. 12:95 already scopes `keyAgreement` to recovery shares and HPKE. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
close_reason: FIXED per notes/review/reconciliation.md: spec/02-identity.md §2.1 l49 keyAgreement only for out-of-group HPKE, KeyPackage init/leaf encryption keys fresh per KeyPackage and unrelated to DID document; spec/05-messaging.md l57 same; no "source of init keys" text remains
